instructions: Think about your child over the past month. For each moment, pick the ONE answer that sounds most like your child right now, even if more than one fits. There are no wrong answers: every choice is a strength.
frequency_stem: In the past month, how often does your child...

scenarios.prompt: A rainy afternoon with nothing planned. Your child is most likely to...

options.text: make up a story, or ask you to read one
sort, count, or set up a game with rules
draw, or build something tall with blocks

scenarios.prompt: At the park, your child is most likely to...

options.text: climb, run, or dig in the sand
sing, or make up a chant while they swing
find the other kids and start a game

scenarios.prompt: On a slow evening walk, your child is most likely to...

options.text: walk along quietly, lost in their own thoughts
stop to look at bugs, leaves or birds
ask a big question, like where heaven is

scenarios.prompt: After you read a story together, your child...

options.text: tells it back, or makes up a new ending
acts it out, or builds something from it
goes quiet, then brings it up days later

scenarios.prompt: On a car ride, your child is most likely to...

options.text: count trucks, read signs, or keep track of the turns
sing along or tap out a beat
watch for cows, horses or birds out the window

scenarios.prompt: At church or Sunday school, your child loves...

options.text: the coloring page or the craft
seeing friends and talking with everyone
asking questions about God and the Bible story

scenarios.prompt: At bedtime, your child wants to...

options.text: hear one more story, or tell you all about their day
sing a song, or have you sing one
pray, and ask you big questions about God

scenarios.prompt: With a new game or puzzle, your child...

options.text: wants to know every rule and how to win
wants the whole family to play
likes to work on it alone, at their own pace

scenarios.prompt: Give your child a big empty box and they turn it into...

options.text: a house or a rocket they plan and decorate
a fort to climb into, or a car to push around
a home for a pet, or for the bugs they found

scenarios.prompt: When family or friends come over, your child...

options.text: tells them everything, with lots of details
plays host and makes sure everyone is included
wants to show them the garden, the pets or a bug jar

scenarios.prompt: Helping you in the kitchen, your child loves to...

options.text: measure, count and do the steps in order
stir, pour, knead and get their hands in it
talk with you about big things, like why God made us

scenarios.prompt: Playing alone in their room, your child is most likely to...

options.text: draw, build, or arrange things just so
sing, dance or play music
daydream, look at books, or simply think

frequency.text: play with words: new words, rhymes or long stories
count, sort, or ask how something works
draw, build, or notice shapes and where things go
want to touch, move or make things with their hands
sing, hum or keep a beat
notice how others feel and want to play together
want quiet time to play or think on their own
notice or ask about plants, animals or the weather
ask big questions about God, heaven, or right and wrong
